convoLines.text: "What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"Being a truck driver taught me to read people fast — who's lying, who's scared, who needs a job. Turns out that's a survival skill. Who knew."
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Since Bridget died... I keep expecting to see Bridget at the fire. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Bridget said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Vito grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Vito is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire feels smaller without Bridget. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Will you help me clean it?"
"Every day it's angrier. I need it cleaned before it turns — I can't work a wound like this. Wrap it tight when you're done."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Bridget owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"Sleep's gone strange. I tend the fire without being asked at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"Hey — A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now."
"Still on what you're hoping for."
"You want me to follow you into the dark? Earn that first."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"I dreamed Bridget was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them Wood Sorrel — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I greet everyone by name each morning. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Vito sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
Vito seems lighter — something good landed recently.
They grin when they spot you — unguarded, for once.
"What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about?"
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
"I can do husbandry. Not well — well enough that nobody's died from it yet. That's my whole résumé now: nobody's died from it yet. Thank you for asking."
"Still on what you're good at. Worth considering."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Bridget is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Vito is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

«Правильно.» They nod back, a little quicker this time.

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Bridget Xu is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Bridget is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.
d41: 🕯️ Bridget Xu is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Bridget kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Bridget's gone." Vito looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Bridget." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Bill blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Tireless Stride (Level 1). You walk like water downhill — no wasted steps, no wasted breath. Every mile costs 15% less.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Bridget Xu, 41 days. The mantle passes to Bill Popov.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Bill Popov, 37 — a barber. His hands know different work now: The Touch, Green Whisper, Turncoat.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Bridget — and Bridget is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Vito, Wei, Dmitri and 1 more speak for Bill — "Bridget trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Bill before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
